newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Min Xin to list joint venture bank unit.
newsitem.headline: Min Xin to list joint venture bank unit.

text.p: Chinese investment company Min Xin Holdings Ltd planned to list its joint venture Xiamen International Bank and was eyeing infrastructural and property projects on the mainland, company officials said on Wednesday.
"We've applied for listing and are waiting for approval," chairman Chen Yuan Kui told a news conference.

Min Xin is the major shareholder in Xiamen International Bank with a 36.75 percent stake. Foreign shareholders are the Manila-headquartered Asian Development Bank and The Long Term Credit Bank of Japan Ltd, each with 10 percent.

The Fujian branch of the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China holds 18.75 percent, Fujian Investment and Enterprise Corporation 12 percent, Construction and Development Corp 7.5 percent and Sino Finance Group Co Ltd 5.0 percent.
The bank is widely expected to list in Hong Kong when the go-ahead is given, but Min Xin officials declined to specify where the listing would be made, if overseas at all.
"The fact that it's the first Chinese-foreign joint venture bank...may be a cause for the delay," Chen said, but he forecast that the unit would enjoy steady growth in the coming few years.
Teaming up with foreign partners was an advantage as the bank could tap their exposure and experience in international dealings, he said.
Chen said the Fujian-based company also planned to invest in infrastructure and property projects on the mainland.
"We are trying to invest in infrastructural projects in China, ports, roads, power stations," he added.
The company has already completed the construction of two roads in Fujian province at a total cost of 18 million yuan.
The company on Tuesday announced net profit of HK$43.68 million in the six months to June 30, up 54.83 percent from the previous year.
